ukmt-imc-2016-02.title: Distance from 1
ukmt-imc-2016-02.body:
The distances from 1 are $\frac18$, $\frac17$, $\frac1{10}$, $\frac1{11}$ and $\frac1{10}$. The smallest is $\frac1{11}$, so $\frac{10}{11}$ is closest.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{10}{11}$**

ukmt-imc-2016-03.title: Evaluate
ukmt-imc-2016-03.body:
The values are $5, 13, 25, 41, 61$. All are prime except $25=5^2$. So exactly one is not prime.

**Answer: (B) 1**

ukmt-imc-2016-03.title: Spot the famous one
ukmt-imc-2016-03.body:
$3^2+4^2=5^2=25$ (the 3-4-5 triangle) is not prime. Checking the others: $5$, $13$, $41$ and $61$ have no factors other than 1 and themselves. So the answer is 1.

**Answer: (B) 1**

ukmt-imc-2016-04.title: Lowest common multiple
ukmt-imc-2016-04.body:
Today is a Thursday and she bakes today. She bakes every 5 days, and Thursdays come round every 7 days. Both happen together again after the lowest common multiple of 5 and 7, which is $35$ days.

**Answer: (E) 35**

ukmt-imc-2016-04.title: List the days
ukmt-imc-2016-04.body:
Count weekdays forward by 5 each time from a Thursday: $5$ days on is Tuesday, $10$ Sunday, $15$ Friday, $20$ Wednesday, $25$ Monday, $30$ Saturday, $35$ Thursday. So 35 days.

**Answer: (E) 35**

ukmt-imc-2016-05.title: Distance from the half-way sign
ukmt-imc-2016-05.body:
The half-way sign is $200-3\frac12=196\frac12$ miles from Edinburgh. Being half way, the whole journey is $2\times196\frac12=393$ miles.

**Answer: (A) 393**

ukmt-imc-2016-05.title: Think about the 400
ukmt-imc-2016-05.body:
If the first sign were half way, the journey would be 400 miles. The real half-way point is $3\frac12$ miles nearer Edinburgh, so each half is $3\frac12$ miles shorter than 200, and the whole is $400-7=393$ miles.

**Answer: (A) 393**

ukmt-imc-2016-06.title: Use thirds
ukmt-imc-2016-06.body:
Goats are one third and sheep two thirds, so there are twice as many sheep as goats. The difference, 12, is one third of the flock. So the flock has $3\times12=36$ animals.

**Answer: (C) 36**

ukmt-imc-2016-06.title: Algebra
ukmt-imc-2016-06.body:
Let there be $g$ goats and $s=2g$ sheep. Then $s-g=g=12$, so the total is $3g=36$.

**Answer: (C) 36**

ukmt-imc-2016-07.title: Angle sum of a hexagon
ukmt-imc-2016-07.body:
The figure is a (non-convex) hexagon. Let its reflex angles be $z^\circ$ (at the $75^\circ$ vertex) and $y^\circ$ (at the $x^\circ$ vertex), so $z=360-75$ and $y=360-x$. The interior angles of a hexagon add to $720^\circ$:
$$27+24+y+23+26+z=720.$$
Also $75+z+x+y=720$. Comparing, $75+x=27+24+23+26=100$, so $x=25$.

**Answer: (C) 25**

ukmt-imc-2016-07.title: Walk around the boundary
ukmt-imc-2016-07.body:
Walk once round the boundary of the hexagon. The total amount you turn is $360^\circ$. At each of the four pointed corners ($27^\circ, 24^\circ, 23^\circ, 26^\circ$) you turn by $180^\circ$ minus the angle. At the two dents the interior angles are reflex ($360-75$ and $360-x$), so there you turn the other way, by $180-75=105^\circ$ and $180-x$ degrees. So
$$(153+156+157+154)-105-(180-x)=360,$$
that is $620-285+x=360$, so $x=25$.

**Answer: (C) 25**

ukmt-imc-2016-08.title: Estimate
ukmt-imc-2016-08.body:
$2.017\times2016\approx4066$ and $10.16\times201.7\approx2049$, so the answer is about $2017$; only E is close.

**Answer: (E) 2017**

ukmt-imc-2016-09.title: Metres per minute
ukmt-imc-2016-09.body:
19.6 s is just under a third of a minute, so Bertie covers about $3\times5.5=16.5$ m per minute, i.e. about $16.5\times60=990$ m per hour $\approx1$ km per hour.

**Answer: (C) 1**

ukmt-imc-2016-09.title: Convert m/s
ukmt-imc-2016-09.body:
Speed $\approx\frac{5.5}{19.6}\approx0.28$ m/s. Multiply by $3.6$ to get km/h: $0.28\times3.6\approx1.0$ km/h.

**Answer: (C) 1**

ukmt-imc-2016-10.title: Find the angles
ukmt-imc-2016-10.body:
$x+5x+2x+4x=360$, so $x=30$, and the angles in order are $30^\circ, 150^\circ, 60^\circ, 120^\circ$. The angles $30^\circ$ and $150^\circ$ are at the two ends of one side and add up to $180^\circ$, so the two sides leaving that side are parallel (co-interior angles). So the quadrilateral has a pair of parallel sides. All four angles are different, so it is not a parallelogram, rhombus or kite (those have a pair of equal angles), and no angle is reflex, so it is not an arrowhead. It is a trapezium.

**Answer: (E) trapezium**

ukmt-imc-2016-10.title: Eliminate
ukmt-imc-2016-10.body:
With angles $30, 150, 60, 120$: a parallelogram or rhombus needs opposite angles equal ($30\ne60$); a kite needs one pair of opposite angles equal; an arrowhead needs a reflex angle. Only the trapezium remains, and indeed $30+150=180$ gives parallel sides.

**Answer: (E) trapezium**

ukmt-imc-2016-11.title: The band of eight squares
ukmt-imc-2016-11.body:
The horizontal row of eight squares in the middle of the net folds into a band around the solid (the left edge of the leftmost square joins the right edge of square E). In a band of 8 squares, the square opposite $P$ is 4 squares along from it. Counting along the row from $P$: B is 2 along, C is 3, D is 4. So D is opposite $P$ and faces up.

**Answer: (D) D**

ukmt-imc-2016-11.title: Visualise the solid
ukmt-imc-2016-11.body:
The rhombicuboctahedron has three "belts" of 8 squares each. The middle row of the net is one belt; opposite faces in a belt of 8 are 4 apart. Starting at $P$ and moving right: square, B, C, D — D is the fourth, so it is opposite $P$. (A is above/below B, not in this belt.)

**Answer: (D) D**

ukmt-imc-2016-13.title: Add all seven lines
ukmt-imc-2016-13.body:
Each corner circle (holding 1 to 7) lies on two lines, and each middle circle (8 to 14) lies on one. So the seven line totals add to $(1+2+\cdots+14)+(1+2+\cdots+7)=105+28=133$. Each line total is $133\div7=19$.

**Answer: (B) 19**

ukmt-imc-2016-13.title: Check it can be done
ukmt-imc-2016-13.body:
With total 19, the corners next to 14 must add to 5, next to 8 must add to 11, and so on. Going round the figure, the corners (starting from the top one, then clockwise past 10, 9, 8, 14, 13, 12, 11) can be $6, 3, 7, 4, 1, 5, 2$: e.g. $6+10+3=19$, $3+9+7=19$, $7+8+4=19$, $4+14+1=19$, $1+13+5=19$, $5+12+2=19$, $2+11+6=19$. A computer search shows this is the only filling.

**Answer: (B) 19**

ukmt-imc-2016-14.title: Set up equations
ukmt-imc-2016-14.body:
Let there be $g$ girls and $b$ boys. Tegwen has $g-1$ sisters and $b$ brothers, so $b=g-1$. A brother has $g$ sisters and $b-1$ brothers, so $g=\frac32(b-1)$. Then $b+1=\frac32(b-1)$, $2b+2=3b-3$, $b=5$, $g=6$, total $11$.

**Answer: (D) 11**

ukmt-imc-2016-14.title: Test the options
ukmt-imc-2016-14.body:
Tegwen's condition means there is one more girl than boys, so the total is odd: $2b+1$. Try 11: 5 boys and 6 girls. A brother has 6 sisters and 4 brothers, and 6 is 50% more than 4. ✓ (For 9: 4 boys, 5 girls, a brother has 5 sisters and 3 brothers — not 50% more.)

**Answer: (D) 11**

ukmt-imc-2016-15.title: Pythagoras
ukmt-imc-2016-15.body:
Let the side of the square be $2x$. The centre is the midpoint of the bottom edge (by symmetry). A top vertex is $x$ across and $2x$ up from the centre and lies on the circle, so $x^2+(2x)^2=1$, giving $x^2=\frac15$. The area is $(2x)^2=4x^2=\frac45$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac45$ cm$^2$**

ukmt-imc-2016-15.title: Eliminate by size
ukmt-imc-2016-15.body:
A square with an edge through the centre and two vertices on the circle has its top corners at distance 1 from the centre, so its side $s$ satisfies $s^2+\left(\frac s2\right)^2=1$, $\frac54s^2=1$, $s^2=\frac45$. (Note area 1 is impossible: then the corner would be at distance $\sqrt{1+\frac14}>1$.)

**Answer: (A) $\frac45$ cm$^2$**

ukmt-imc-2016-16.title: Prime factors of 24
ukmt-imc-2016-16.body:
$24=2^3\times3$. A multiple of 24 must contain at least $2^3$. Only the last number does, and it also contains 3. So exactly one.

**Answer: (B) 1**

ukmt-imc-2016-16.title: Divide by 8
ukmt-imc-2016-16.body:
Each number contains a factor 3, so the question is which are divisible by 8. The first three contain only $2^2=4$ and the rest of the factors are odd, so they leave remainder 4 on division by 8. Only the fourth, with $2^3$, works.

**Answer: (B) 1**

ukmt-imc-2016-17.title: Equal areas
ukmt-imc-2016-17.body:
Let the dashed circle have radius $r$. Then $\pi\cdot14^2-\pi r^2=\pi r^2-\pi\cdot2^2$, so $196-r^2=r^2-4$, $2r^2=200$, $r=10$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 10 cm**

ukmt-imc-2016-17.title: Average of squares
ukmt-imc-2016-17.body:
The area inside a circle is proportional to $r^2$, so the dashed circle's $r^2$ must be halfway between $2^2=4$ and $14^2=196$: $r^2=100$, $r=10$.

**Answer: (B) 10 cm**

ukmt-imc-2016-18.title: Pythagoras
ukmt-imc-2016-18.body:
Let the equal sides be $x$ and the hypotenuse $y$; $y^2=2x^2$. Then $x^2+x^2+y^2=4x^2=72$, so $x^2=18$, and the area is $\frac12x^2=9$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: (C) 9 cm$^2$**

ukmt-imc-2016-18.title: Half of the total
ukmt-imc-2016-18.body:
By Pythagoras the square on the hypotenuse equals the other two together, so it is half of 72, i.e. 36: the hypotenuse is 6. The triangle is a quarter of the square on its hypotenuse (draw both diagonals of that square), so its area is $36\div4=9$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: (C) 9 cm$^2$**

ukmt-imc-2016-19.title: Count numbers above the median
ukmt-imc-2016-19.body:
The mode 9 means at least two 9s; the mean 10 means at least one number above 10. So at least three numbers exceed 8. With median 8, at least three numbers are at most 8, so the list has at least 6 numbers. Six works: $1, 2, 7, 9, 9, 32$ has median $\frac{7+9}2=8$, mode 9 and mean $60\div6=10$.

**Answer: (B) 6**

ukmt-imc-2016-19.title: Rule out five
ukmt-imc-2016-19.body:
Suppose the list had 5 numbers $a\le b\le c\le d\le e$. The median is $c=8$, and the mode 9 needs at least two 9s, which can only be $d$ and $e$. Then the sum is $a+b+8+9+9=50$ (mean 10), so $a+b=24$; but $a, b\le8$, so $a+b\le16$. Contradiction. Fewer than 5 numbers fails for the same reason (there is no room for two 9s and a big number). So 6 is the smallest, and $1, 2, 7, 9, 9, 32$ works.

**Answer: (B) 6**

ukmt-imc-2016-20.title: A 3-4-5 triangle
ukmt-imc-2016-20.body:
The rectangle is 10 cm wide and 8 cm tall, and each semicircle has its diameter along a 10 cm side, so radius 5 cm. Let $O$ be the centre of the lower semicircle, $A$ an intersection point of the semicircles and $B$ the centre of the rectangle. By symmetry $AB$ is horizontal at half the height, so $OB=4$ and $OA=5$; the triangle $OBA$ is right-angled at $B$, so $AB=3$. The width of the overlap is $2\times3=6$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 6 cm**

ukmt-imc-2016-20.title: Coordinates
ukmt-imc-2016-20.body:
Put $O=(0,0)$; the lower semicircle is $x^2+y^2=25$ and the upper is $x^2+(y-8)^2=25$. Subtracting, $y=4$, and then $x^2=9$, $x=\pm3$. The width is $6$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 6 cm**

ukmt-imc-2016-21.title: Cut into squares, rectangles and triangles
ukmt-imc-2016-21.body:
Let the side be $a$ and let $b$ be the legs of the corner right-angled isosceles triangles, so $a^2=2b^2$. The octagon is a central $a\times a$ square, four $a\times b$ rectangles and four corner triangles (two of which make a $b\times b$ square).
- Shaded trapezium: one rectangle and two triangles $=ab+b^2=b^2(1+\sqrt2)$.
- Whole octagon: $a^2+4ab+2b^2=2b^2+4\sqrt2b^2+2b^2=b^2(4+4\sqrt2)$.

Ratio $=(1+\sqrt2):4(1+\sqrt2)=1:4$.

**Answer: (A) 1 : 4**

ukmt-imc-2016-21.title: Cut into horizontal strips
ukmt-imc-2016-21.body:
With $a$ and $b$ as before ($a=\sqrt2b$), the octagon is the shaded trapezium on top, an identical trapezium at the bottom, and a middle rectangle of width $a+2b$ and height $a$.
- Trapezium: parallel sides $a$ and $a+2b$, height $b$, area $\frac12(2a+2b)b=(a+b)b=(\sqrt2+1)b^2$.
- Rectangle: $(a+2b)a=(\sqrt2+2)\sqrt2b^2=(2+2\sqrt2)b^2$, which is exactly two trapezia.

So the octagon has the area of $1+1+2=4$ trapezia, and the ratio is $1:4$.

**Answer: (A) 1 : 4**

ukmt-imc-2016-22.title: What liars and truth-tellers need
ukmt-imc-2016-22.body:
Write T for a truth-teller and L for a liar. Each T must have an L on both sides. Each L is lying, so at least one neighbour is a T — and two neighbouring L's cannot be both next to another L, so no three L's in a row.
- Most T's: alternate TLTL…, which closes up since 2016 is even: $1008$ T's.
- Fewest T's: LLTLLT…, which closes up since 3 divides 2016: $672$ T's.

Difference $=1008-672=336$.

**Answer: (E) 336**

ukmt-imc-2016-22.title: Blocks
ukmt-imc-2016-22.body:
Between consecutive T's there are 1 or 2 L's (at least 1 because a T needs liar neighbours, at most 2 because an L needs a T neighbour). So the circle is made of blocks TL and TLL. With $k$ blocks the number of people is between $2k$ and $3k$, so $672\le k\le1008$, and $k$ is the number of truth-tellers. Difference $336=\frac{2016}{6}$. (A brute-force check for 12 people gives 6 and 4, difference $2=\frac{12}{6}$.)

**Answer: (E) 336**

ukmt-imc-2016-23.title: Pythagoras twice
ukmt-imc-2016-23.body:
Let the arcs have radius $R$ and the small circle radius $r$. Two adjacent arcs meet at the tips of the design, which are 2 cm apart, and each arc is a quarter circle, so the angle at an arc's centre between its endpoints is $90^\circ$: $R^2+R^2=2^2$, $R=\sqrt2$.

The centres of the four arcs form a square around the small circle's centre; two adjacent arc centres are $2R$ apart (the arcs touch where they meet), and the small circle touches both. By symmetry the angle at the small circle's centre between two adjacent arc centres is $90^\circ$, so $(R+r)^2+(R+r)^2=(2R)^2$, giving $R+r=\sqrt2R=2$. So $r=2-\sqrt2$.

**Answer: (B) $2-\sqrt2$**

ukmt-imc-2016-23.title: Coordinates
ukmt-imc-2016-23.body:
Put the small circle's centre at the origin with the four tips at $(\pm1,\pm1)$ (the design is 2 cm wide). The arc joining $(1,1)$ and $(-1,1)$ is a quarter circle, so its centre is at $(0,2)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt2$. The nearest point of this arc to the origin is $(0,2-\sqrt2)$, and the small circle touches the arcs there, so $r=2-\sqrt2$.

**Answer: (B) $2-\sqrt2$**

ukmt-imc-2016-24.title: Add the speeds
ukmt-imc-2016-24.body:
Let the escalator length be $d$. The escalator moves at $\frac d{60}$ per second and Aimee walks at $\frac d{90}$ per second. Together: $\frac d{60}+\frac d{90}=\frac{3d+2d}{180}=\frac d{36}$ per second, so it takes 36 seconds.

**Answer: (C) 36**

ukmt-imc-2016-24.title: Pick a length
ukmt-imc-2016-24.body:
Say the escalator has 180 steps. The escalator moves 3 steps per second and Aimee walks 2 steps per second, so together 5 steps per second: $180\div5=36$ seconds.

**Answer: (C) 36**

ukmt-imc-2016-25.title: Compare tile areas
ukmt-imc-2016-25.body:
A hexagon of side $2s$ splits into 6 equilateral triangles of side $2s$, each of which splits into 4 triangles of side $s$. So one hexagon has the area of 24 small (black) triangles. In the pattern there are two black triangles for every hexagon (each hexagon touches 6 triangles and each triangle touches 3 hexagons). So black : grey $=2:24=1:12$, and the black fraction is $\frac1{13}$ (approximately, since the floor is finite).

**Answer: (D) $\frac1{13}$**
